transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
Once I start talking, I just can’t seem to stop. I feel like I have to get every idea out all at once, and people keep telling me I’m overwhelming them.
Do these periods of rapid talking and racing thoughts come and go in distinct phases, or is this something you have experienced constantly since childhood?

No, this isn't something I've dealt with since childhood; it actually just started about two months ago after I got a big promotion at my startup. Before this whole super-charged phase kicked in, my mood and the way I talked felt completely normal.
Have you ever had periods in the past where you felt the exact opposite—such as feeling very depressed, down, or losing interest in things for weeks at a time?
No, I haven't really experienced times like that where I felt deeply depressed or lost interest in things. Before all of this started, my mood was generally pretty stable and normal.
Have you ever had a previous period, even a brief one, where you felt this same kind of high energy, decreased need for sleep, or rapid thoughts before this current episode started?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like this before. This is the very first time I've ever felt this way, with my thoughts racing and having so much energy. Before this started a couple of months ago, my life and my sleep were completely normal.
During these past two months, have you noticed a decreased need for sleep, such as feeling fully rested and energized after only a few hours of sleep?

Yes, absolutely—for the past two months, I've been waking up after only two or three hours of sleep feeling completely wired and energized. I feel like I physically cannot sit still, so I end up pacing around or starting new projects even when I try to get my brain to shut off.
To help rule out other causes, are you currently taking any new medications, using recreational drugs, or consuming unusually high amounts of caffeine or stimulants?

I’m not taking any new medications or recreational drugs at all. I do drink some coffee during my late-night work sessions, but it's nothing unusual or beyond my normal routine. I definitely haven't been taking any stimulants or other substances.
Have you noticed yourself making any impulsive decisions, spending large amounts of money, or taking risks that you wouldn't normally take during this time?

I haven't really been spending large amounts of money or taking dangerous physical risks. However, I have done some impulsive things like booking networking trips on a whim as part of my busy schedule. It is more about trying to keep up with all my big ideas than doing anything reckless.
Has this high-energy state caused any severe disruptions or major problems at your work or in your relationships, or have you required hospitalization because of it?

Yes, it has caused huge disruptions. At work, I've been pulled off key projects, banned from speaking on client calls, and HR strongly urged me to get this urgent evaluation because I was derailing meetings and overwhelming my team. My friends have also started backing away because they find me exhausting and unpredictable, and while I haven't been hospitalized, things have definitely reached a crisis point.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a first-lifetime, distinct episode of manic symptoms lasting for two months. Symptoms include pressure of speech, racing thoughts, a severely decreased need for sleep (feeling fully rested after 2-3 hours), psychomotor agitation (pacing, inability to sit still), and mild impulsivity. This episode has caused significant functional impairment at work (HR intervention, removed from client calls) and in social relationships. There is no history of depressive episodes, and substance-induced mania has been ruled out. The presentation is consistent with a manic episode without psychotic symptoms (F30.1).
